text: Coco favours soft, low-angle or diffused light: golden hour, sunrise haze, blue-hour dusk, and window light raking through shutters or arches. Midday works only for turquoise water shot from above. Her grade is warm and filmic. Highlights are creamy, never clipped. Whites lean ivory. Saturation is restrained except for signature hues like terracotta, turquoise and saffron. Skin is natural and warm, never orange. Greens are olive, not neon. Blacks are deep in interiors and night scenes but lifted and hazy in airy landscapes. She shoots almost everything vertical (2:3). Compositions are centred and symmetrical, with receding arches, corridors or a single strong subject, and big calm skies or water as negative space, the horizon kept level. People are small and placed (a lone figure in a courtyard, a swimmer at a pool edge) or seen from behind. Food is shot close at three-quarter angle with shallow depth of field and a hand in action. Mood: quiet, unhurried, lived-in luxury. Avoid harsh flash, HDR, cluttered crowds and posed tourist grins.
prefer: Golden hour, sunrise haze, dusk or soft window light; directional side light through shutters/arches
One clear subject, centred or on a strong symmetry axis (arches, corridors, pool edges)
Generous negative space: pale sky, still pool water, sea filling the top or bottom third
Level horizons and straight verticals in architecture
People small in the frame, turned away or mid-gesture, giving scale to a place
Food at a 3/4 angle with shallow depth of field, a hand lifting noodles or plating, and the table context blurred behind
Elevated views down onto coves, pools and terraced landscapes
Warm creamy highlights with detail held in whites and skies
Textured, tactile surfaces: plaster, timber, stone, linen, rattan
Night shots that keep inky blacks with warm lantern pools of light
avoid: Hard, flat midday light on faces or interiors
Blown highlights or pure digital white skies
Over-saturated, neon greens or electric blues; HDR or crunchy clarity
Tilted horizons and converging verticals in architecture
Busy, cluttered frames with no clear focal point or with crowds facing the camera
Direct on-camera flash and cold fluorescent casts
Posed, grinning, camera-facing tourist portraits; heavy skin smoothing
Top-down flat-lay food shots with no human or place context
Wide horizontal snapshots with an empty centre
film_vs_digital: Her film work (35mm compact, e.g. Contax G/T-series) has visible grain, gentle halation and soft contrast: colour frames drift to pastel cyan water and cream skies, and her black-and-white self-portraits use hard slatted sun and deep, inky blacks. Her digital work is cleaner and slightly more saturated, with crisper focus and shallow depth of field on food and details, but it is graded to imitate the film look: warm highlights, muted greens and a slight matte.
edit_notes: Pick the edit with warmer, creamier highlights (ivory not blue-white), held highlight detail, and restrained saturation where olive and teal greens are muted while signature colours (terracotta, turquoise, lantern amber) stay rich. In bright outdoor scenes, prefer a gently lifted black point with a hazy matte feel. In interiors and at night, prefer deep, true blacks and moody contrast. Reject edits that look clinical, HDR, neon-saturated, or that push skin orange or magenta.
